documents.title: Conductor invariance of the positivity scan
documents.source_line: ** [`rh12.html`](../rh12.html) — §4 "Dig three — the family: gears wearing characters"
header: **Source:** [`rh12.html`](../rh12.html) — §4 "Dig three — the family: gears wearing characters"

> Nothing in the arc's machinery is special to ζ. … Built here from Hurwitz zeta (Euler–Maclaurin, validated against three exact identities including ψ′(¼) = π² + 8G), the L-functions of the real primitive characters mod 3, 4, 5 are anchored absolutely — L(2,χ₄) equals Catalan's constant to 10<sup>−10</sup>, and independently the ℤ[i] lattice sum over 1.1 million points reproduces ζ(2)·G to 3×10<sup>−5</sup> … Zeros: 151, 162, 170 ordinates to height 250, against counting-formula predictions of 150.6, 162.1, 170.8; first ordinates 8.039737 (χ₃) and 6.020949 (χ₄) matching the cited values to 10<sup>−5</sup>, and 6.648453 (χ₅) measured. The explicit formula: re-verified per character to 10<sup>−5</sup> … The scan: Weil positivity per character, nonnegative across the range for all three, dips to 2.5×10<sup>−5</sup> (χ₃), 1.6×10<sup>−2</sup> (χ₅), 1.2×10<sup>−1</sup> (χ₄) — floor depths set by each spectrum's local gaps, exactly as for ζ.
- χ₃, χ₄, χ₅ are the real primitive Dirichlet characters of conductors 3, 4, 5; G is Catalan's constant; G = β(2).

documents.title: λ* = −2.27×10⁻⁵ at altitude 10⁶
documents.source_line: ** [`rh12.html`](../rh12.html) — §3 "Dig two — altitude: GUE arrives, and the pairs are harvested"
header: **Source:** [`rh12.html`](../rh12.html) — §3 "Dig two — altitude: GUE arrives, and the pairs are harvested"

> The headline: **λ* = −2.27×10⁻⁵**, fifty-two times past rh11's −0.00119, three decades past rh10's −0.989. And with it, the hunt's complete economics, now measured rather than argued: the bound is quadratic in the rarest gap; the rarest gap among N samples shrinks like N<sup>(−1/3)</sup>; so λ* improves like N<sup>(−2/3)</sup>, and *each further decade costs 10^1.5 ≈ 32× more zeros*.
The three tightest harvested pairs collide at λ* = −2.3×10<sup>−5</sup>, −3.2×10<sup>−5</sup>, −4.8×10<sup>−5</sup>, each on the g²/8 law to 0.1%.

documents.title: The explicit formula as a Lefschetz ledger
documents.source_line: ** [`rh12.html`](../rh12.html) — §6 "What would render a base: the three constructions"
header: **Source:** [`rh12.html`](../rh12.html) — §6 "What would render a base: the three constructions"

> The ledger. Deninger's proposal reads the explicit formula as a transversal Lefschetz fixed-point formula for a flow: closed orbits at the primes with period log p, the archimedean place as the fixed point at infinity, the zeros as the spectrum of the infinitesimal generator on an H¹ that does not yet exist. The formula itself, of course, exists — it is the arc's equation (1) of rh10 — and re-organized in orbit form it balances on our table to 2×10−5 … the pole term (+50.5, the H⁰/H² poles at 0 and 1), the archimedean term (−20.4, the place at infinity), and one closed orbit per prime (−29.9 total, period log p, k-fold traversals weighted p(−k/2)) balance the spectral side (0.17) to 2×10−5.
- Orbits are indexed by the primes with period log p, and k-fold traversals weighted p<sup>(−k/2)</sup>.

documents.title: The Castelnuovo ledger, and every minor
header: > Weil's actual inequality on C × C is Castelnuovo–Severi's: for a correspondence, σ(D∘D′) ≤ 2·d(D)d′(D) — degree terms dominate the self-pairing, with the defect controlled by the Hodge index. … the **pole terms** h(±i/2) are the degree terms … the **archimedean integral** is the fiber at infinity … the **gear sum** is the intersection with the Frobenius graphs … and the **spectral side** — forced nonnegative if RH — is the defect.

computed as: Fejér (pole +50.48, archimedean −20.42, orbits −29.89, defect +0.172), a Gaussian at the dip (defect +2.6×10<sup>−2</sup>), and rh12's optimal window (defect +9.6×10<sup>−6</sup>); "each ledger balances against the independently computed spectral side to 6×10<sup>−4</sup>". And:

> all 300 Cauchy–Schwarz ratios |G<sub>jk</sub>|/√(G<sub>jj</sub>G<sub>kk</sub>) of the crossing form, by node distance: everything inside the bound with margin (worst 0.705; worst normalized 2×2 minor +0.50). A single point above 1 would be a negative 2×2 minor — a refutation of RH computable in one line.

documents.title: The nested-slice exhaustion is positive
documents.source_line: ** [`rh14.html`](../rh14.html) — §4 "The exhaustion: finite slices of one continuous form"
header: **Source:** [`rh14.html`](../rh14.html) — §4 "The exhaustion: finite slices of one continuous form"

> Toeplitz slices G[j,k] = E(y<sub>j</sub>−y<sub>k</sub>) at four nested (support, mesh) levels — 49, 99, 99, 199 dimensions, meshes 0.06 and 0.03, supports 3 and 6 — all positive, with λ<sub>min</sub> falling monotonically along both nesting directions (1.3×10⁻⁸ → 6.6×10⁻¹⁰ → 2.3×10⁻¹¹) exactly as the variational principle demands of a single continuous form exhausted by finite slices, and never through zero.

- Refine the mesh (hats of width 0.06 are exact sums of hats of width 0.03) and widen the support; the space of windows grows, and the union over all meshes and supports is dense in every space of admissible windows.

documents.title: The horizon law: σ_k²·v² ≈ 3.9×10⁻³, the same at every mesh
header: > And the prediction errors, which do decay, decay according to one law that does not mention the mesh at all: σ<sub>k</sub>² ~ c/k² in the index, which is c/v² in the physical horizon v = kΔ, with measured c = 3.91×10⁻³, 4.23×10⁻³, 3.48×10⁻³ across the three meshes — a 22% spread over an 8× change in Δ.
> The three recursions — 198, 398 and 798 steps at three different meshes — fall on one curve of slope −2. The mesh cancels; what is left, σ²v² ≈ 3.9×10⁻³, is a property of E itself.

documents.title: The widest positivity certificate (support 6, mesh 0.015, 60-digit arithmetic)
documents.raw_status: ** VERIFIED (numerical, 60-digit arithmetic; for a kernel correct to 10⁻⁹)
header: **Status:** VERIFIED (numerical, 60-digit arithmetic; for a kernel correct to 10⁻⁹)

> Support **6** at mesh **0.015** — 799 nodes, the kernel out to v = 11.97, gears to e¹² — run through (4) in **60-digit arithmetic**: all 799 prediction errors positive, max|ρ<sub>k</sub>| = 0.301754, σ<sub>798</sub>² = 2.14×10⁻⁵. Not "positive to within rounding": positive as a fact about the computed kernel, with the floating-point question removed from the discussion.
and the source's own honest form of a certificate (§6):

> the honest form of a certificate is *"the recursion at mesh Δ stays inside the unit disc to depth n, for a kernel correct to 10⁻⁹, with margin 0.40–0.70"* — a statement that would become unconditional under interval arithmetic on the same quadrature, which is a finite amount of engineering and no new mathematics.
